## Step-by-Step Implementation Plan:

### 1. Create the Main Car Body
- Create a box with dimensions 200mm (X) × 100mm (Y) × 100mm (Z)
- This will serve as the base shape for the car body

### 2. Create the Windshield Cutout
- Create another box with dimensions 50mm (X) × 100mm (Y) × 50mm (Z)
- Position this box at one edge of the main body to represent the windshield area
- This box will be subtracted from the main body to create the windshield recess

### 3. Subtract the Windshield from the Body
- Use a boolean difference operation to subtract the windshield box from the main body
- This creates the recessed windshield area

### 4. Create the Wheels
- Create four cylinders, each with:
  - Radius: 25mm
  - Height/Thickness: 10mm
  - Orientation: Along the Y-axis
- The wheels need to be positioned at the four bottom corners of the car body

### 5. Position the Wheels
- Place the wheels at the following positions:
  - Front-left wheel: X = -100mm (left edge), Z = -50mm (bottom)
  - Front-right wheel: X = -100mm (left edge), Z = -50mm (bottom), but on opposite Y side
  - Rear-left wheel: X = +100mm (right edge), Z = -50mm (bottom)
  - Rear-right wheel: X = +100mm (right edge), Z = -50mm (bottom), but on opposite Y side
- The wheels should be embedded into the body, creating half-cylinder shapes
- Y-axis positioning: Two wheels at Y = -50mm (negative Y side) and two at Y = +50mm (positive Y side)

### 6. Union All Components
- Combine the modified car body with all four wheels using boolean union operations
- This creates the final toy car model

The key considerations:
- The wheels are oriented along the Y-axis (pointing inward from both sides)
- They're positioned to be half-embedded in the body
- The windshield cutout creates a realistic detail on the car body
